subject: POC / Trial plan — deployment mode decision (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps — deployment modes & PoC

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery:

- Current workload: customer support summarization + search reranking for support articles (~250 req/s peak, avg 40 tokens per response).
- Primary concerns: latency SLO <=150ms p95 for user-facing flows, data isolation for customer PII, and predictable monthly cost.
- Deployment options discussed: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool, predictable throughput), Private (VPC/on-prem — required only if data residency or strict KMS controls are needed).

From our call it sounds like Acme is leaning toward Dedicated capacity for predictable latency/cost, but you want to validate via a 4-week PoC to confirm throughput and latency under production-like load and confirm KV cache behavior.

Proposed next steps:
1) Redwood to deliver a PoC plan (success criteria, test harness, infra config) — see attached initial draft (acme-poc-plan.pdf).
2) Acme to confirm stakeholders and legal/IT contacts for any network/KMS requirements.
3) Schedule a short kickoff with engineering (30 min) — propose Thurs 11/12 or Mon 11/16.

Success criteria (draft):
- p95 latency <=150ms for 95% of requests under peak simulated load (250 req/s)
- Token-level cost estimate within 20% of forecast
- KV cache hit rate >=60% for prefix-heavy queries
- Integration checklist: VPC peering and KMS access validated (if we go Private)

I'm attaching a short comparison doc that highlights the tradeoffs between Dedicated and Private deployments.

Can you confirm the right IT contact for network/KMS and whether Acme requires a Private deployment baseline (vs. try Dedicated first)?

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Great — thanks for confirming Tom. Attached is the finalized PoC plan (I've updated success criteria and added a timeline). High level:

- PoC duration: 4 weeks (11/17 — 12/15)
- Phase 1 (Week 0): environment setup — Dedicated pool provisioned, test dataset ingestion, VPC peering validated for KMS
- Phase 2 (Week 1-2): functional validation — routing, KV cache tuning, baseline latency measurements
- Phase 3 (Week 3): load testing to 250 req/s peak, observability/trace validation
- Phase 4 (Week 4): runbook handoff, cost forecast, decision point

Final success criteria (we agreed):
- p95 latency <=150ms for 95% of sampled test windows at peak
- End-to-end throughput >=250 req/s without error rate >1%
- Cache hit rate >=60%
- Signed-off security checklist by Lisa/IT (KMS access validated)

Kickoff agenda (30 min):
- Introductions & roles (5m)
- PoC timeline & success criteria (5m)
- Network/KMS requirements (10m)
- Autoscaling & burst capacity settings (5m)
- Next steps & action owners (5m)

Action items before kickoff:
- Rajiv (IT) to confirm KMS and VPC peering details (rajiv.patel@acmecorp.com)
- Ben/Jordan (Redwood) to confirm Dedicated pool sizing and preliminary autoscale policy
- Tom/Lisa to share any sample dataset access methods (S3 link, redaction notes)

We're including Ben and Jordan on the kickoff so they can answer technical questions about Dedicated sizing and autoscale.

See you Monday — calendar invite sent.

Thanks,
Marissa
